subject.title: feat(agents): derive fallbacks from configured model catalog

question: Should OpenClaw accept a new opt-in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacksFromModels` config contract for text-model failover, or should catalog/provider-family fallback design stay in the broader fallback product thread?
rationale: The implementation direction is plausible, but it adds public config and provider-routing behavior; automation should not choose that permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept after repair
options.body: Accept the narrow opt-in only after the branch aligns embedded-run fallback availability with candidate derivation and includes real failover proof.

options.title: Defer to broader fallback design
options.body: Pause or close this PR in favor of deciding provider-family, wildcard/auto, and catalog-derived fallback semantics together in the broader issue.

options.title: Keep explicit fallbacks only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and keep `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` as the supported way to define ordered failover.

recommendation.title: Accept after repair
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow opt-in only after the branch aligns embedded-run fallback availability with candidate derivation and includes real failover proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal for the model fallback resolver and embedded failover boundary.
